title: I will playtest your game and give honest feedback
author: Psychological-Arm42
selftext:
I have a lot of buffer time between prompts while my game is being built on my second monitor. I would like to help the community by playtesting your games / demos, for free, and giving, honest, critical feedback from a gamer's perspective. No sugarcoating, Just highlighting what feels good and what feels off, what I liked and what I didn't like. 

Drop your games, I'm bored lol

replies.author: kakashi_sakurai
replies.body:
The moving controls actually annoyed the ever loving shit out of me lmao. Like it made it borderline unplayable on my phone. When you rack up enough xp to level a skill, it takes away your controls, and then throws you back into the game instantly after you pick. That’s well and fine, but now I have to slap my finger back where I want the virtual control without looking. That’s well and fine too, but when you get closer to the halfway point near the end of the level, there’s way too much shit going on to look at my finger placement, so at that point muscle memory should take care of where to put my finger and all that. Except I can’t rely on that because the stupid janky controls are floating all over the screen lmao. Wherever the control starts, it should stay there unless I lift my finger. Having the whole thing drag when I move my finger out of bounds has never been a thing in any mobile game with virtual analogs. Please get rid of that lol. It was actually driving me borderline insane lmao. Also the arrow spamming is kinda excessive too, like waaaayyy too excessive. Then making the range enemies also back up from you is also annoying. Like they’re already op when half my screen is arrows. Why do they also need a defensive strategy as well? I had fun with it for what it was, but it was also ping ponging me back and forth between fun and pure annoyance.

ALSO, why does the first character use pure range attacks, then the next one is melee based? That’s also kinda backwards lol. I didn’t know I was signing up for a nerf.

comments.author: Conscious-Season-607
comments.body:
Thanks for offering this, that’s generous. I’d love a blunt read on mine.

**Brave the Descent** is a free turn-based roguelike on itch.io: you chain same-coloured orbs into attacks, lead a small squad, and push through a branching map of fights, elites, shops and bosses. First game, still early; the art and most of the audio are AI-generated (the page lists the tools) and it's still early and rough.

[https://encryptedsolar.itch.io/brave-the-descent](https://encryptedsolar.itch.io/brave-the-descent)

The page has the Act 1 build right now (a Windows download, plus a browser version). I’m putting up v0.2.0 very soon, with Act 2 and a new Leader, so if you’d rather test the newer one, check back later today.

Three things I’d most like your gamer’s view on:

1. Is the orb chain clear in the first fight, or do you have to work it out?
2. Does the default combat speed feel too slow? (There’s a speed setting, but I’m unsure about the default.)
3. What made you want to stop, if anything did?

  
Also, if you dont mind sharing what you're working so I can try it too? it's the least I can do

comments.author: New_Complaint5282
comments.body:
Cosmonoid, a paddle roguelite. Brick breaking with run leveling, so you pick cores, mods and powers, evolve them, and at the end there's a three-phase boss. Chapter 1 is playable in the browser, nothing to install: https://cosmonoid.vercel.app  
PC only for now, mouse and keyboard.  
On effort: it started as a single-file prototype I tuned over dozens of logged runs. I've been building it into a proper game since early October, and it's on the 11th tester build now. So far only friends have played it, and friends are polite. That's why I'm after honest subjective feedback, especially the parts that feel unfair or boring ;)  
There's a feedback key on the title screen, but a reply here works just as well.  
Happy to playtest others too, tag me.
